P1.desc: omphalocele vs gastroschisis: sac (present/absent) + herniated viscera (bowel+liver vs bowel only) · แยกจากรูป

P2.desc: associated anomalies: omphalocele common 50% (cardiac, chromosomal, BWS) vs gastroschisis uncommon <10% (atresia)

P3.desc: location: umbilicus (cord inserts into sac) vs right of umbilicus (normal cord)

P4.desc: mode of delivery: omphalocele vaginal/cesarean vs gastroschisis vaginal (ERNICA 37–39 wk)

P5.desc: surgical management: omphalocele nonurgent (sac protects) vs gastroschisis urgent

P6.desc: prognostic factors: omphalocele = associated anomalies · gastroschisis = condition of bowel (complex)

P7.desc: omphalocele pathophysiology: failure of viscera to return to abdominal cavity

P8.desc: gastroschisis: ventral body fold theory — failure of lateral fold migration, more on right

P9.desc: prenatal omphalocele: USG by GA 18 wk · membrane-covered, not free-flowing · cord inserts into omphalocele

P10.desc: prenatal gastroschisis: USG by 20 wk · free-floating bowel · defect right of normal cord · IUGR

P12.desc: initial: wrap bowel in warm saline-soaked gauze + non-evaporating wrap (plastic bag)

P13.desc: initial: IV access + fluid resuscitation · OG decompression · empirical ATB

P14.desc: initial: thorough exam for intestinal atresia / associated anomalies

P15.desc: gastroschisis: immediate primary repair vs silo-assisted delayed closure with serial reduction

P16.desc: omphalocele: primary repair · staged closure · escharification (paint and wait)

P17.desc: approach abdominal pain: H&P → localized pain / gut obstruction / peritonitis / with mass

P18.desc: RUQ: choledochal cyst, cholecystitis, gallstone, liver tumor/abscess, right pyelonephritis

P19.desc: epigastric/LUQ: pancreatitis, peptic ulcer, gastric volvulus · splenic abscess/torsion, left pyelonephritis

P20.desc: periumbilical: GI duplication, enteritis, mesenteric cyst, internal hernia, mesenteric lymphadenitis

P21.desc: RLQ: appendicitis, Meckel's diverticulitis, dysmenorrhea, ovulation, PID, ovarian tumor torsion, ureteric stone

P22.desc: hypogastric/LLQ: ruptured appendicitis, dysmenorrhea, ovulation · constipation, ovarian torsion, stone

P24.desc: extreme age <5 yr prone to rupture

P25.desc: presentation: nonspecific pain, migratory to RLQ, fever, N/V, anorexia, diarrhea

P26.desc: PE: tender RLQ McBurney's point, guarding, fever

P27.desc: Ix: leukocytosis + left shift · USG · CT diameter > 6 mm

P29.desc: labs: CBC, UA ± BUN Cr Elyte · UPT if teenage female

P30.desc: PAS components (cough/percussion/hop RLQ 2, RLQ tenderness 2, others 1) · ≥6 suggests

P31.desc: Alvarado components (rebound 1, fever >37.3, WBC >10,000 = 2, left shift >75%) · ≥7 suggests

P32.desc: PAS tiers: <4 low (imaging may not be warranted) · 4–6 US first then CT · >6 surgical consult

P34.desc: algorithm: uncertain → observation/USG → not seen → CT → not seen → observation or diagnostic laparoscopy

P35.desc: ruptured appendicitis: IV ATB + IV fluid → peritonitis without mass → appendectomy

P36.desc: peritonitis with RLQ mass → non-surgical → improved → interval appendectomy 6–8 wk

P37.desc: not improved 24–48 hr → USG → phlegmon → appendectomy · abscess → appendectomy/percutaneous drainage

P38.desc: Meckel rule of 2s (2%, 2 ft from ICV, 2 in, male 2×, 2 ectopic tissue gastric/pancreatic)

P39.desc: Meckel presentations: diverticulitis · obstruction (intussusception, omphalomesenteric band internal hernia) · LGIB (ectopic gastric)

P40.desc: vitelline remnants: Meckel, fibrous cord, umbilical sinus, vitelline cyst, umbilical fistula

P41.desc: Meckel Tx: diverticulitis → diverticulectomy ± resection · obstruction → laparotomy · LGIB → scan + diverticulectomy/segmental resection

P42.desc: Tc-99m pertechnetate scan detects heterotopic gastric mucosa

P43.desc: intussusception = most frequent cause of bowel obstruction in infants/toddlers · peak 4–9 months

P46.desc: intermittent sudden cramping pain + currant jelly stool + palpable mass

P47.desc: AXR: dilated SB loops + RUQ soft tissue mass near hepatic flexure

P49.desc: non-operative: NG decompression, IV fluid, air contrast enema

P50.desc: enema contraindications: free air, peritonitis, refractory hypotension

P51.desc: operative: failed/incomplete reduction, peritonitis, lead point, pneumoperitoneum

P52.desc: acute scrotum surgical: torsion of testis · incarcerated/strangulated indirect inguinal hernia

P53.desc: torsion typical <3 yr or after puberty

P54.desc: presentation acute severe unilateral scrotal pain (on-off), swelling, erythema, N/V, urinary sx, fever

P55.desc: absent cremasteric reflex (present does not exclude)

P56.desc: enlarged, retracted upward, transverse orientation, negative Prehn's sign · compare contralateral

P57.desc: clinical diagnosis · U/A not needed · Doppler only if Dx in question · don't delay surgery for imaging

P58.desc: TWIST: swelling 2, hard 2, absent cremasteric 1, N/V 1, high-riding 1 · ≤2 low · 3–4 medium · ≥5 high

P60.desc: goal OR within 6 hr · never delay assuming nonviability

P61.desc: viable → detorsion + orchiopexy · not viable → orchiectomy

P63.desc: recovery 1–2 wk · one functional testis sufficient for fertility
